Our financial results have been, or are expected to be, impacted by several significant trends and activities, which are described below.
We expect that the trends described below may continue to impact our results of operations, cash flows, and financial position.
We expect to realize the most recent $20-per-ton increase on incremental fall sales.
Following the close of the fall fill order window, we increased the Trio ® list price by $30 per ton to $440 per ton, reflecting our constructive market outlook.
We expect the higher price to be reflected in remaining spot sales during the fourth quarter.
In turn, we generally have increased inventory levels in the third and fourth quarters in anticipation of expected demand for the following year.
Based on our ongoing engagement with the NMSLO and the history of our operations, we believe we will be successful in obtaining a long‑term renewal of the easement.
In July 2025, we drilled a sample well into one of the lowest sections of the AMAX mine; however, the brine pool anticipated based on our imaging was not present.
During 2026, we continued permitting activities and the technical evaluation of AMAX project, and we made the decision to defer additional capital investment until at least 2027.

While the AMAX cavern remains a key part of our HB mine and we remain confident in the potash reserve in place, we have adequate brine sources to maintain production at our HB facility for the next few years.

Before committing additional capital, we are working to ensure we have adequate brine injection volumes to flood the AMAX cavern, which will be the largest cavern in the HB system, and the necessary bitterns management system in place to maximize the full potential of this additional cavern.
The 2026 adjustment was attributable to the weighted-average carrying cost per ton of certain potash inventory at our HB facility exceeding its forecasted net realizable sales value.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded lower of cost or net realizable value inventory adjustments of $1.3 million in our potash segment because the weighted average carrying cost per ton for inventoried potash products exceeded their forecasted average net realizable sales.
When we arrange and pay for freight, our quotes and billings are based on expected freight costs to the points of delivery.
We operate our potash and Trio ® facilities at production levels that approximate expected demand and consider current inventory levels and expect to continue to do so for the foreseeable future.

Our principal production costs include labor and employee benefits, maintenance materials, contract labor, and materials for operating or maintenance projects, natural gas, electricity, operating supplies, chemicals, depreciation and depletion, royalties, and leasing costs.

We expect that our labor and contract labor costs in Carlsbad, New Mexico, will continue to be influenced most directly by the demand for labor in the local region where we compete for labor with another fertilizer company, companies in the oil and gas industry, and a nuclear waste processing and storage facility.

We evaluate our deferred tax assets and liabilities each reporting period using the enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the periods in which the deferred tax liability or asset is expected to be settled or realized.
We expect to make capital investments in 2026 of approximately $45 million, with the majority of this being sustaining capital.
We anticipate our 2026 operating plans and capital programs will be funded out of operating cash flows and existing cash.
We continue to evaluate our expected sources and uses of cash and may modify our capital as determined by our Board.

We may also seek additional liquidity through debt or equity financings, subject to market conditions and the terms of our existing revolving credit facility, although there can be no assurance that such financing will be available on acceptable terms, or at all.

Based on our current cash balances, availability under our revolving credit facility, and the expected cash flows from operations, we believe we have sufficient liquidity to meet our obligations for at least the next twelve months.
Any repurchases will be made at our discretion and will depend on market conditions, liquidity, applicable securities laws, and other factors.

We are seeing supportive pricing alongside improving demand for both of our product categories and expect these conditions to carry into the spring 2027 planting season.
The Company intends to continue evaluating opportunistic share repurchases while maintaining financial flexibility to invest in initiatives that enhance the long-term earnings power of the business.

We have raised our consolidated capital expenditure guidance for the full year 2026 to approximately $45 million and w e plan to invest an additional $16 million in 2027 as part of an overall plan to deliver an additional 30 thousand tons of annual Trio ® production above first half 2026 run rates.
We have begun to realize some of the benefit from these investments in late 2026 and expect to realize the full impact next year.

Beyond this investment, the Company has a roadmap for a potential additional ~100 thousand tons of annual production with modest additional investment and expects to discuss these opportunities in more detail in the future.
